### 1. What the customer expresses, and how the simulator behaves

The caller (found by name through `find_customers`, `full_name="Renata Villalobos"` →
`customer_id ecfd6c45-7f23-4d30-bd7a-494a80364ede`) states the target object, the timing and the
authorisation mode clearly, and leaves the boundary of the action to the desk:

- Target object — "the care plan she bought in 2024 alongside her platinum engagement ring"; "she
  wants to end the plan and get back whatever part of it she has not used".
- Timing — "plainly wanting this finished today rather than sometime next week"; she moves abroad on
  6 October. So: act now, not wait.
- Boundary — she does **not** fix it: "She is content for the agent to do whatever the account needs
  on her behalf, putting it as *you sort it out, I just want it closed*."
- Authorisation — one firm constraint on the money: "whatever money comes back should go out as a
  cheque to the address on file, because the card she paid on was closed last year". And she performs
  her own confirmations: "Where the agent hands her something to confirm in her own name, she does it
  there and then".

The simulator only conveys needs and answers conditionally. Every load-bearing fact is gated on being
asked: "Only if she is asked does she say where the ring actually is"; "Only if she is asked does she
say that she has kept up the check-ups on it"; "She volunteers nothing about anything outstanding on
the plan, because she has never thought about it and would not know where to look." It executes a
user-owned tool only when handed one. It never pushes the procedure along. This is passive, script-
bounded behaviour with no policy or GT leakage; the two numeric things she says ("about fifteen
hundred of cover left", "she had imagined something nearer five hundred") are both offered *after*
the agent has spoken and are both explicitly disclaimed ("without offering any view of her own about
what it should be"; "does not press a number of her own").

Identity: she can supply mobile `3125553247`, DOB `1971-04-09`, postal code `60614`, email
`r.villalobos@northbranchmail.com`. `verify_customer_identity` needs two agreeing details besides the
customer reference — reachable. She has no reference numbers of any kind, so every id must be found
from her profile. Reachable: `find_protection_plans(customer_id=…)` returns the one plan.

**(a) The benefit the accepted claim `CL-320742` draws** — `record_claim_settlement_8eb9093c`,
`benefit_amount`.

Worksheet: `benefit_drawn_on_an_accepted_claim_94946301`.

- *Step 1 — claim and work order.* "The claim being answered is the one last entered against the plan,
  and the work order it was sent in on is the one carrying that claim's reference." → `CL-320742`,
  `WO-321065`.
- *Step 2 — the figure standing for the repair.* Baseline: "the labour and the parts charged on the
  work order" (= 945.00). Tiered by `figure_standing_for_a_covered_repair_5e4d0280`: "Where the work
  order carrying the claim's reference shows no date the bench finished the work and carries a ceiling
  the customer authorised above zero, the figure standing for the repair is that authorised ceiling."
  `WO-321065` has `completed_date ''` and `authorized_total 1325.0`. **Tier 1 → 1325.00.**
  (Query return that puts her on this tier: the `find_service_orders` row above.)
- *Step 3 — wear.* "reduced for the years the piece has been worn, at the coverage's annual reduction
  for each whole year since the piece was sold … the whole years between the day the piece was sold
  and the handling date, part years dropped." Sale date read from the plan record
  (`conditions_for_writing_coverage_f043b419`: "the date the piece was sold is read from the plan
  record") = 2024-07-19 → **2 whole years**.
  Rate tiered by `annual_wear_reduction_rates_613cfaa2`: "Where the most recent inspection entry on
  the plan records the piece as sound and that work order records no rework, the annual reduction is
  taken at the sound-piece share, being 0.5 of the rate the coverage publishes." Most recent
  inspection entry = 2026-05-12, `inspection_result 'pass'`; `WO-321065` `rework_count 0`.
  Published rate for the 3-Year plan = 6.0 percent (table in that document). **Tier 1 → 3.0 percent.**
  Reduction = 2 × 3.0 % = 6.0 % of 1325.00 = 79.50 → **1245.50 left**.
- *Step 4 — what the coverage answers for.* Baseline: "the whole of what is left". Tiered by
  `share_of_bench_work_answered_for_by_service_level_5459dc4e`: "Where the service level the work runs
  at targets fewer business days than the coverage's own turnaround target and the coverage offers
  expedited handling, the coverage answers for 0.9 of what is left." The coverage's own target
  (3-Year) = 12 business days and expedited handling = yes (table in that document, corroborated by
  `included_services_and_workshop_handling_6b0715f3`). The work runs at `Master Jeweler Service` of
  the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service, whose target is 10 business days
  (`docs/service/turnaround_targets_and_bench_queue_bf98326b.json`). 10 < 12. **Tier 1 → ×0.9 →
  1120.95.**
- *Loyalty — **not assembled by the worksheet**.* `loyalty_discount_on_covered_bench_work_7d6cd72c`
  states: "Where a claim under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans is answered by bench
  work, the figure standing for the repair is reduced once for loyalty … Where the customer's
  membership stands active and the qualifying spend recorded since its tier took effect is at or above
  the spend that tier must be maintained by, the reduction is the loyalty discount the service level
  the work runs at carries." Her membership is active; the spend recorded since the tier took effect
  is 8420.00 against the Belrose Circle Gold maintenance qualifying spend of USD 5000.00
  (`docs/circle/tier_qualification_schedule_224954b8.json`), so 8420.00 ≥ 5000.00. **Tier 1 → the full
  loyalty discount of the level the work runs at**, which for `Master Jeweler Service` is 5 percent
  (`docs/service/member_labour_discount_and_protection_work_admission_2244bae0.json`).
  **The worksheet `benefit_drawn_on_an_accepted_claim_94946301` contains no step for this reduction at
  all** — steps 1–7 are claim/work order, figure, wear, what the coverage answers for, what the
  customer bears, the two limits, rounding — and it carries no "order and rounding" clause pinning how
  the reductions assemble (the other four computation documents in this corpus each carry one). So the
  visible materials leave two defensible assemblies, which do **not** agree:
  - loyalty taken sequentially on the figure the step before it leaves:
    1325.00 × 0.94 × 0.95 × 0.9 = **1064.9025 → 1064.90**;
  - loyalty taken, like wear, as a percentage *of the figure standing for the repair* (which is how
    the factor document words its base — "the figure standing for the repair is reduced once for
    loyalty"), so the two reductions are 6 % + 5 % of 1325.00:
    (1325.00 − 79.50 − 66.25) × 0.9 = 1179.25 × 0.9 = **1061.325 → 1061.33/1061.32**.
  I record **1064.90** as the reading I would take, because every other reduction in this corpus is
  assembled sequentially and the sibling computation documents say so explicitly; but I record that
  the visible materials do not close it. **This is a blind-audit finding, not a rollout slip.**
- *Step 5 — what the customer bears.* Baseline: "the coverage's deductible on the claim". Tiered by
  `deductible_borne_on_a_settled_claim_822dc1a0`: "Where no settlement entry stands on the plan inside
  that window [the 12 whole months to the handling date] and the whole months since the most recent
  inspection entry are within the coverage's inspection interval, nothing at all is charged to the
  customer." The only settlement on the plan was booked 2025-09-02, outside 2025-09-17→2026-09-17;
  the most recent inspection entry is 2026-05-12, 4 whole months back, against a 6-month interval.
  **Tier 1 → `deductible_charged` = 0.00.** (Baseline would have been 50.00.)
- *Step 6 — the two limits.* "limited to the coverage's share of the item value recorded at purchase"
  = 100.0 percent of 12400.00 (rate card
  `allowances_deductibles_claim_limits_81077974`) = 12400.00; "and to the benefit still standing on
  the plan, which is the allowance granted and reinstated in the 12 whole months ending on the
  handling date, less the benefit consumed by the settlements booked in those same 12 months" =
  2500.00 (the 2026-07-19 reinstatement) − 0.00 (no settlement in the window) = 2500.00. Neither
  binds.
- *Step 7 — rounding.* Two decimals once at the end, never below zero.

**→ `benefit_amount` = 1064.90 ; `deductible_charged` = 0.00.**

*Note on the customer's "about fifteen hundred".* The plan record's `remaining_benefit_allowance` is
1520.0 and the app shows ≈1500. The visible KB closes this boundary: the second limit is defined in
the worksheet as the allowance granted and reinstated in the 12 whole months less the settlements in
those same 12 months (= 2500.00), and the older reading of the remaining allowance is carried in
`each_plan_answers_for_its_own_piece_887d6129` explicitly as **no longer in force** — "The benefit
consumed in the current coverage year on one plan is read as the sum of the settlements booked to that
plan in that year, and the remaining allowance is the granted allowance less that sum." So her figure
is excluded by a visible sentence, and neither limit binds on either reading.

**(b) The premium returned on cancellation** — `confirm_plan_cancellation_48603509`, `refund_amount`.

Worksheet: `premium_returned_on_cancellation_9b559b86`.

- *Step 2 — premium paid toward the plan.* "the premium entries booked to it, net of the give-backs
  booked against them" → 1364.00 − 120.00 = **1244.00** (corroborated by `premium_paid_to_date 1244.0`).
- *Step 3 — the months still to run.* Baseline: "the coverage's term in months less the whole months
  since the plan was bought and less the month in progress. The whole months since the plan was bought
  are counted to the handling date."
  - The *whole months since the plan was bought* are tiered by
    `months_coverage_has_run_while_at_the_workshop_223c9d8c`: "Where that work order shows no date the
    piece was handed back and carries a promised date later than the handling date, the whole months
    since the plan was bought are counted to that promised date". `WO-321065` (the order carrying the
    reference of the claim last entered) has `delivered_date ''` and `promised_date '2026-09-25'`, which
    is after 2026-09-17. **Tier 1 → count 2024-07-19 → 2026-09-25 = 26 whole months** (26 months after
    2024-07-19 is 2026-09-19, which 2026-09-25 has passed; 27 would need 2026-10-19).
  - The *formula* is tiered by `months_of_term_still_to_run_and_the_inspection_record_4d9f43e3`:
    "Where the whole months since the most recent inspection entry are within the coverage's inspection
    interval and the plan has run beyond its first coverage year of 12 months, the months still to run
    are the coverage's term less the whole months since the plan was bought, the month in progress
    counting as still to run." Most recent inspection 2026-05-12 → 4 whole months, within the 3-Year
    interval of 6; 26 > 12. **Tier 2 → 36 − 26 = 10 months still to run.**
- *Step 4 — the proportion.* 10 of a term of 36 → 1244.00 × 10/36 = **345.555556**.
- *Step 6 — how much of the unused premium comes back.* Baseline: "The whole of that unused premium is
  returned." Tiered by `share_of_unused_premium_returned_after_claims_8fc68819`: "Where a settlement
  entry stands on the plan inside that window and the benefit drawn in it is below that share of the
  yearly benefit allowance, 0.75 of the unused premium is returned." After the settlement of
  `CL-320742` is booked today, a settlement entry **does** stand inside the 12 whole months to the
  handling date, and the benefit drawn in that window is 1064.90, below 0.5 × 2500.00 = 1250.00
  (the yearly benefit allowance of the 3-Year plan, table in that document). **Tier 2 → ×0.75 →
  259.166667.** (On the alternative loyalty assembly, 1061.33 is also below 1250.00, so the tier —
  and therefore this figure — is the same.)
- *Administration fee.* Baseline: "less the coverage's administration fee" (25.00 for the 3-Year plan,
  `premium_cancellation_renewal_terms_3cfe77b4`). Tiered by
  `cancellation_administration_fee_charged_3e4c1f5d`: "Where the calendar days since the plan was
  bought are beyond that window and the customer's membership tier carries a qualifying spend it must
  be maintained by, the administration fee is charged at the member share, being 0.5 of the fee the
  coverage publishes." 2024-07-19 → 2026-09-17 is far beyond the 30-day full-refund window; Belrose
  Circle Gold carries a maintenance qualifying spend of USD 5000.00. **Tier 2 → 12.50.**
- *Step 7 — order and rounding.* "the administration fee is taken off only after that share has been
  applied. The figure is rounded to two decimal places once at the end" → 259.166667 − 12.50 =
  246.666667 → **246.67**.

**→ `refund_amount` = 246.67 ; `refund_channel` = `mail_check`** ("a cheque is posted to the address
on the profile" — she is firm that "whatever money comes back should go out as a cheque to the address
on file").

*Her "nearer five hundred" is excluded* by the visible proportion step: only 10 of 36 months stand to
run, so no reading of this worksheet reaches 500.

### 5. Tool sequence executable on the spot, owners, dependencies, terminal state

1. `find_customers(full_name="Renata Villalobos")` — agent, read. → `customer_id`.
2. `verify_customer_identity(customer_id, phone_number="3125553247", date_of_birth="1971-04-09", …)`
   — agent, write. Required first: "Identity must be cleared before any money is moved, any agreement
   is changed and any record of the customer's is written."
3. `find_protection_plans(customer_id)` → the plan id and variant.
4. `find_protection_ledger(protection_plan_id)` → the two claim references, the entry on which each
   loss was entered, the allowance and premium entries, the inspections.
5. `find_service_orders(customer_id)` / `find_service_ledger(customer_id)` → `WO-321065`, its
   authorised ceiling, its promised date, its rework count, its service level.
6. `find_circle_memberships(customer_id)` → tier, standing, qualifying spend.
7. **`record_claim_settlement_8eb9093c`** — agent, write. `protection_plan_id da7ae772-…`,
   `claim_reference 'CL-320742'`, `source_entry_id 'b803ba2d-26a7-411f-8f38-5589c47c6b87'` (the
   `protection_claim_filed` entry), `benefit_amount 1064.90`, `deductible_charged 0.00`.
   *Forward dependency:* it is this entry that puts a settlement inside the 12-month window and so
   fixes the share in (b). *Backward dependency:* none.
8. **`confirm_plan_cancellation_48603509`** — **user**, write; handed over with
   `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and run by the customer ("Ending coverage they paid for is the
   customer's alone to do, so the cancellation is confirmed by the customer on the protection service
   request record"). `protection_plan_id da7ae772-…`, `refund_amount 246.67`,
   `refund_channel 'mail_check'`. *Backward dependency:* step 7 must already stand.
- **Terminal state:** the coverage record reads `cancelled` with today as its closing date; a
  cancellation stands confirmed on the protection desk's request record; a premium-returned entry of
  246.67 stands in the coverage history; `CL-320742` stands answered by a settlement of 1064.90 with
  nothing borne by the customer; the plan's count of claims settled has gone to 2.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**The list of problems, and the direction of the dependencies.**

```
  [root, the only thing the customer asked for]
  P1  Give up the live coverage and take the premium back
        ▲ waits on
  P2  Answer the claim standing open against the coverage (settle CL-320742)
```

**Handling order:** P2 → P1.

**Hop P1 ← P2 — marked `state-derived`.**

*The sentence.* `cancellation_of_live_coverage_c4827af3` (the document of the problem that is
blocked), second paragraph, standing on its own:

> "The premium returned is fixed only after the benefit consumed by every claim entered against the
> plan stands recorded against it."

It names a **state** of the record ("the benefit consumed … stands recorded against it") and an
ordering connective ("only after"). It names no tool, no other policy, no action and no performer.

*The query return that shows the state does not hold.* `find_protection_ledger(protection_plan_id=
da7ae772-…)` returns, among the twelve entries, this one and no entry answering it:

> `{'claim_reference': 'CL-320742', 'claim_type': 'stone_loss', 'claim_outcome': 'not_applicable',
> 'event_type': 'protection_claim_filed', 'posted_date': '2026-08-28', 'amount': 1900.0,
> 'service_order_reference': 'WO-321065', 'protection_entry_id':
> 'b803ba2d-26a7-411f-8f38-5589c47c6b87'}`

By contrast the earlier claim does carry its answer — `CL-320411` has a `protection_claim_settled`
entry of −980.00 whose `source_entry_id` points back at the filing. So *some* claim entered against
this plan has no benefit consumed recorded against it, and the sentence's state is unmet.

*Finding the write that brings that state about, from the depended-on documents and the records.* The
words the sentence uses are "the benefit consumed" and "stands recorded against it". Searching the
corpus with the records' own vocabulary — `claim`, `benefit consumed`, `recorded against the
coverage` — reaches `claim_settlement_entries_0180a9d9`, whose own rule says:

> "A claim that a plan … answers for is settled by drawing benefit from the plan the covered piece
> stands on … a settlement entry is written against the coverage under the claim's own reference,
> **carrying the benefit consumed as a movement out of the plan's benefit allowance**…"

That is the write that puts "the benefit consumed" on the record. The alternative answer,
`claim_refusal_entries_585def8f`, expressly does not: "No benefit allowance moves."

*Which of the two answers this claim is.* Decided from the records against
`claim_intake_conditions_4310df55` and `schedule_of_perils_49b7aad2`, not handed over by any pointer:
the claim's `claim_type` is `stone_loss`; the perils schedule shows the Belrose Care Plan 3-Year
answers for "manufacturing defect, prong wear, chain break, clasp failure, **stone loss**" and lists
stone loss among its exclusions only on the Manufacturer Limited Warranty and the 2-Year plan ("A
stone lost from its setting is covered | no | no | **yes** | yes | yes | yes"). The plan stands at
`active`, and "A claim is opened only while the covering plan stands at active or inspection
overdue". `settlement_conditions_and_claim_limits_4c3d6df9` clauses 1–3 are all satisfied: the benefit
standing (2500.00) covers it; no settlement stands against `CL-320742`; the rolling-twelve-month cap
of 3 is not reached (no settlement booked since 2025-09-02) and the 45-day minimum interval since the
most recent settlement is long past. So the claim is **settled**, not refused.

**Nothing remains.** Repeating the same reasoning on P2: the documents of the settlement problem
(`claim_settlement_entries_0180a9d9`, `benefit_drawn_on_an_accepted_claim_94946301`) state no sentence
saying its result waits on anything, and the records show nothing outstanding that would block it.

**No hop is `pre-solved`.** No document of P1 names `record_claim_settlement_8eb9093c`, names the
settlement policy, tells the reader to "settle the claim first", or lays out a route. The cancellation
hub names only its own tool, in its own invocation block. The settlement documents carry no sentence
disclosing that a cancellation waits on them (checked by reading all 53 documents: the sentence at
`cancellation_of_live_coverage_c4827af3` occurs once in the corpus and nowhere else).

### Two-way counter-proof

**The visible materials fully support the conclusion reached.** Every quantity above was read from a
titled document or a tool return, both cited at the point of use.

**The closest alternative starting points, and the visible sentence or record that excludes each.**

**Where the source leaves a boundary open, the documents leave it open too.** One boundary is *not*
closed by the visible materials and I record it here as openness rather than as a settled reading: the
**assembly position and base of the loyalty reduction** in the settlement worksheet (see §4(a)). The
worksheet has no step for it and no order clause; the factor document says only that "the figure
standing for the repair is reduced once for loyalty". Two defensible assemblies give 1064.90 and
1061.33/1061.32. I cannot tell, blind, whether this openness is the source's or the rendering's.

**Counter-proof on the problem tree — the natural wrong answer.** "She asked only to close the plan,
so close the plan." Doing only that leaves the governed result in a state the visible principles do
not allow, for a reason visible without any policy knowledge:

- `cancellation_of_live_coverage_c4827af3` states that what comes back "is worked out from what they
  have actually paid toward the plan and the part of the term they will not now use", and that "The
  premium returned is fixed only after the benefit consumed by every claim entered against the plan
  stands recorded against it."
- `find_protection_ledger` shows a claim entered against this plan (`CL-320742`, 2026-08-28) with no
  entry recording what benefit it consumed.
- Therefore the premium returned is **not yet fixed**, and a cancellation run now would book a figure
  the coverage's own terms say cannot yet be worked out. It would also be materially wrong: with no
  settlement inside the 12-month window, `share_of_unused_premium_returned_after_claims_8fc68819`
  would give the whole of the unused premium (345.56 − 12.50 = 333.06) instead of 0.75 of it (246.67).
- `confirm_plan_cancellation_48603509` moreover closes the coverage so that "no further claim can be
  opened on it", so the claim could not be answered afterwards.

The exclusion rests on a prerequisite sentence standing on the blocked side plus a tool query — the
source's own form — and on no pre-solved statement.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back numbers.**

- *Settlement, reading only `benefit_drawn_on_an_accepted_claim_94946301` and the product figures it
  names:* figure standing = labour + parts on `WO-321065` = 945.00; wear at the published 6.0 percent

- *Refund, reading only `premium_returned_on_cancellation_9b559b86` and the figures it names:*
  1244.00 × (36 − 25 − 1)/36 = 345.555556; the whole of the unused premium returned; less the
  published administration fee 25.00 → **320.56**. Definite, and different from 246.67.

### KB-RUNTIME RED — the loyalty reduction's place in the settlement assembly is not entailed

**Symptom.** The scored `benefit_amount` is not uniquely determined by the visible materials. Reading
the computation document and the factor document together, two assemblies are both defensible and give
different numbers: **1064.90** (loyalty taken sequentially, on the figure the step before it leaves)
and **1061.32/1061.33** (loyalty taken, like wear, as a percentage of the figure standing for the
repair, the two coming off the same base). My blind answer reached 1064.90 only by analogy with the
four sibling computation documents, and I recorded at the time that the corpus does not close it.

**Root cause.** The source's `protection_ext_claim_settlement.rule` closes it with a sentence written
for exactly this purpose, and that sentence has been rewritten in the KB so that it names the
*opposite* base:

- Source rule (and `compute_basis.discounted_work`):
  > "**The reduced figure, and not the figure before any loyalty discount, is the base every later
  > step acts on.**"
  with `compute`: `discounted_work: repair_figure * (1 - loyalty_pct / 100)` and
  `worn_work: discounted_work * MX(0, 1 - wear_rate_pct * wear_years / 100)`.
- KB `benefit_drawn_on_an_accepted_claim_94946301`, step 2:
  > "**2. The figure standing for the repair.** What an accepted claim draws from the benefit
  > allowance is the priced bench work the repair comes to, taken as the labour and the parts charged
  > on the work order the claim was sent in on. **That figure is the base every later step acts on.**"

In the KB, "that figure" is the priced bench work *before* any loyalty reduction, and the word
"loyalty" occurs nowhere in that document — nor anywhere in the corpus outside the single factor
document `loyalty_discount_on_covered_bench_work_7d6cd72c` (verified:
`grep -i loyalty` over all 53 documents returns hits in that one file only).

**Evidence.**
- `env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/docs/protection/benefit_drawn_on_an_accepted_claim_94946301.json`,
  `content`, numbered steps 1–7: there is no step for the loyalty reduction and no "order and
  rounding" clause. Step 7 is "**7. Rounding.** The figure is rounded to two decimal places once at
  the end, and nothing below zero is ever drawn."
- The four sibling computation documents each *do* carry an assembly clause —
  `amount_recorded_against_a_refused_claim_d428e9b2` step 7, `premium_returned_on_cancellation_9b559b86`
  step 7, `benefit_carried_across_on_transfer_a38b7908` step 5,
  `yearly_benefit_allowance_granted_afresh_e492e334` step 8 — which is what makes the settlement
  document's silence a gap rather than a house style.
- `loyalty_discount_on_covered_bench_work_7d6cd72c` says only "the figure standing for the repair is
  reduced once for loyalty" and "The reduction is taken once"; it never says the reduced figure is the
  base the later steps act on.

**Affected document and location.**
`env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/docs/protection/benefit_drawn_on_an_accepted_claim_94946301.json` —
`content`, step 2 (the rewritten base sentence) and the absence of a loyalty step among steps 1–7.

**Not attributed to the rollout agent.** A solver taking the KB at its word and computing 1061.32 has
read the corpus correctly; the corpus, not the solver, is what fails to entail 1064.90.

**Verdict: KB-RUNTIME RED** (one finding). Every other item of this blind audit — the branch, the
objects, the second scored figure, the owner split, the terminal state and the whole problem tree —
is **PASS**.

revision 1, so this section compares the re-rendered corpus against the revision-1 blind answer, which
stands as written, and against the source.

Corpus audited: `cat env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/docs/protection/*.json | sha256sum` =
`fab5030fbcf6303edc96d2ae7dd5b0a8adf46957bead13c0e2e7872c14dc4722` (was
`d794eb65765cc3246e7b9ceb691bcbb681265eba322ee48f86fee868ecfa2ff7`).

**Scope of change, verified independently of the renderer's claim.** Content of each of the 53
published documents was compared against the frozen revision-1 dump: **exactly one file differs**,
`benefit_drawn_on_an_accepted_claim_94946301.json`; the other 52 are byte-identical in `title` and
`content`, and no file was added or removed. The revision-1 file references and PASS findings
therefore still hold on their own evidence, not on the renderer's say-so. The gate snapshot is
consistent with this: `content[min/mean/max]` moved `1236/2108/3574` → `1236/2113/3574`, min and max
unchanged, the mean moved by the ~229 characters this one document gained (2928 → 3157).

### The revision-1 KB-RUNTIME finding: genuinely closed

The document now runs eight numbered steps, with a new step 3:

> "**3. The loyalty reduction.** Nothing is taken off that figure for loyalty. The reduced figure, and
> not the figure before any loyalty discount, is the base every later step acts on."

and step 2 now ends at "…the work order the claim was sent in on." — the bare restatement "That figure
is the base every later step acts on." is gone.

**(a) The assembly sentence is verbatim, exclusion intact.** Source
`protection_ext_claim_settlement.rule` / `compute_basis.discounted_work`: "The reduced figure, and not
the figure before any loyalty discount, is the base every later step acts on." Document, step 3:
character-for-character the same, including the exclusion "**and not the figure before any loyalty
discount**". Checked by exact substring match of every document sentence against the source rule.

**(b) The new step reads as a default, not as a rule.** "Nothing is taken off that figure for loyalty."
is flat and unconditional — no "where", no tier, no condition from the ladder. It is the same
grammatical form the four sibling computation documents use for their own nil defaults ("Nothing is
met as goodwill."; "The grant carries no membership uplift."; "What carries across is not reduced for
the claims answered on the plan."; "Nothing is taken off the figure for work the coverage would have
answered for without a claim."). It renders `factors[loyalty_reduction].baseline: {loyalty_pct: '0.0'}`
and **not** the ladder's third tier, so the ladder is not leaked into the baseline.

**(c) A reader of the visible corpus alone now reaches exactly one value on task 0's world.**
Recomputed on the records obtained through the tool-shaped path:

| Step | Reading | Figure |
|---|---|---|
| 2 + `figure_standing_for_a_covered_repair_5e4d0280` tier 1 | authorised ceiling on `WO-321065` | 1325.00 |
| 3 + `loyalty_discount_on_covered_bench_work_7d6cd72c` tier 1 | 5 % off; **the reduced figure is the base** | 1258.75 |
| 4 + `annual_wear_reduction_rates_613cfaa2` tier 1 | 2 whole years × 3.0 % of 1258.75 | 1183.225 |
| 5 + `share_of_bench_work_answered_for_by_service_level_5459dc4e` tier 1 | × 0.9 | 1064.9025 |
| 6 + `deductible_borne_on_a_settled_claim_822dc1a0` tier 1 | − 0.00 | 1064.9025 |
| 7 | min with 12400.00 and 2500.00 — neither binds | 1064.9025 |
| 8 | rounded once at the end | **1064.90** |

The rival reading recorded in revision 1 — wear and loyalty both taken as percentages of the same
pre-loyalty 1325.00, giving 1061.32/1061.33 — is now **excluded by the text itself**: step 3 says the
base is the reduced figure "and not the figure before any loyalty discount", so step 4's "That figure"

**(d) The masked fall-back is unchanged and still matches the source's baseline.** Reading only this

**(e) Task 0's second scored figure is unaffected.** 1064.90 is still below 0.5 × 2500.00 = 1250.00, so

**(f) The eight-step order states nothing the source does not pin.** The source's rule fixes four

|---|---|
